subject: Embedding architecture follow-up — BlueHarbor / Redwood
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@blueharbor.ai>, Priya Sharma <priya@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Embedding architecture follow-up — BlueHarbor / Redwood

Hi Alex / Priya — great call today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can spin up a tight POC: 

What we heard (goals)
- Replace Embex-hosted embeddings with Redwood-hosted embeddings + reranker for semantic search and similarity scoring.
- Keep query latency < 60ms median for 100 QPS burst; target cost parity or better versus current vendor.
- Migrate historical index with minimal downtime and validate end-to-end quality.

Open technical items (please confirm):
- Current embedding dimension: you mentioned 1536 — is that correct for both query and doc vectors?
- Normalization: are vectors currently L2-normalized on ingest?
- Batch sizes in your ingestion pipeline today (per worker): you said ~512 — is that a deliberate tuning choice or just current throughput?
- Auth: you indicated token-based API keys; will you need SSO/KMS integration later for the private deployment?
- Routing/fallback: do you want us to route low-latency queries to a smaller model variant during spikes?

Proposed POC scope and next steps
1) Tech kickoff (30–45m) — propose Thu 2027-09-02 10:00am PT — align on data access, migration window, success metrics.
2) Provide SDK + examples for: auth (short-lived API tokens), streaming embeddings, batch ingestion, and model routing policy.
3) Migration approach: dual-write to Embex + Redwood for 2 weeks, backfill historical documents over a streaming job, final cutover with rollback plan.
4) Baseline eval: a small eval suite (100 queries + relevance metrics) to validate parity before cutover.

Attachments: blueharbor_poc_requirements.pdf (POC checklist) and a short tech spec stub in Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c4d5e6f7g8h

Ask: Please confirm the open technical items above and whether 9/2 10am PT works for the kickoff. If that time doesn't work, suggest 9/3 morning PT.

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: blueharbor_poc_requirements.pdf (PDF)]

Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Embedding architecture follow-up — BlueHarbor / Redwood

Marissa — thanks for the clear notes, this is great. Quick answers below and a couple clarifications.

- Dimension: yes, both query and doc vectors are 1536 today (Embex default).
- Normalization: Embex normalizes to unit length (L2) at write time. We currently store float16 vectors.
- Batch size: 512 is what our bulk ingestion jobs use. For online writes (customer uploads) it's much smaller. We would like to move toward smaller batches (64–128) to reduce tail latency during ingestion.
- Auth: currently API key token; for POC API key is fine. At scale we'll want SSO + KMS for key rotation (longer term, private deployment is on the table).
- Routing/fallback: yes, we'd like a fallback plan: route to a smaller model variant for <30ms SLO violations.

Kickoff: 9/2 10am PT works for our team. Can you include engineering and a short agenda? I'll add Isha (data eng) to the thread — she'll own the migration tasks.

Attaching a small Embex export sample for reference: embex_export_sample.csv

Cheers,
Alex
Head of Data Products, BlueHarbor Analytics
[Attachment: embex_export_sample.csv (CSV)]

Thanks for the forward — quick tech plan below. I'm copying the main items into the POC pack and will upload migration snippets to the Drive link before kickoff.

POC deliverables (engineering)
- SDK examples: python/ts snippets for issuing short-lived API tokens (JWT signed by Redwood), and for batch ingestion with configurable batch_size parameter (default recommended: 64). I'll include both streaming (gRPC) and REST/HTTP examples.
- Auth pattern: use short-lived bearer tokens (10m TTL) issued by Redwood control plane; for BlueHarbor POC we'll accept static API keys, but we recommend testing TTL rotation. KMS integration path: we provide KMS hooks for key wrapping (notes in spec).
- Routing: implement a lightweight router in the SDK that checks SLO latencies and switches to a small-variant model (e.g., embed-compact-1) when median response exceeds threshold. We'll provide a routing config file that is editable in their deployment.
- Normalization: keep their current L2-normalized vector semantics; our SDK will re-normalize to float32 on ingest to avoid precision loss during internal ops. We'll include a validation check (dim==1536 && norm within 1e-3 of 1.0).
- Migration: dual-write (Embex + Redwood) for 14 days; backfill historical docs via streaming job (we'll provide a backfill worker sample in migration-snippets.zip). Validate with nightly sampling (compare cosine similarity distribution). Cutover: switch search read path to Redwood + monitor QA suite. Rollback: revert read path to Embex if >5% hit-rate degradation versus baseline.

I'll upload the code bundle (migration-snippets.zip) and a short gist with example router config: https://gist.github.com/redwood/migration-router-abc123

Let me know if you want a deeper write-up before Thu.

—Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
